subject: Onboarding benchmark telemetry dossier and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@tritonlogistics.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@tritonlogistics.com>

Subject: Initial telemetry and acceptance criteria (Triton)

Hey Avery / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed, Triton needs a short, actionable acceptance dossier that our infra team can hand to the ops folks running the preprod load runs. Can you confirm the following so we can lock the schedule for week of Sep 13?

Quick asks:
- Target P50/P95/P99 latency (in ms) for service X (typical request size: 512 tokens)
- Expected sustained throughput (qps) per instance and total qps required for our peak demo (we mentioned ~450 qps)
- Any IP allowlist or test API keys we should provide to our load engineers
- Format for run artifacts — you mentioned a log plus a telemetry snapshot PNG?

We'd like to run two passes: a steady-state 60-minute run and a 30-minute ramp to peak. Can you share the exact acceptance criteria and a template run report that your CS team expects?

Thanks — looking to finalize the calendar today.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole
SRE Lead, Triton Logistics
ethan.cole@tritonlogistics.com
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial telemetry and acceptance criteria (Triton)

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Below is the onboarding benchmark dossier we use for quick handoffs; attaching a one-page load plan (triton-loadplan-v1.xlsx).

High level acceptance targets (service X, request ~512 tokens):
- P50 latency <= 40 ms
- P95 latency <= 120 ms
- P99 latency <= 300 ms (tail latency)
- 99.9th percentile token generation tail <= 450 ms per token (measured separately for long-seq runs)

Throughput guidance:
- Sustained baseline: 150 qps total (cluster-level) for warm traffic
- Peak demo target: 450 qps for 30m ramp (we recommend 3 worker nodes at current config)
- Per-instance expected qps (default model config): ~150 qps (with continuous batching enabled)

Run plan we recommend (what to share back in the run report):
1) Warmup: 15m at 25% of peak (collect KV cache hit rates)
2) Steady-state: 60m at baseline (150 qps)
3) Peak ramp: 30m ramp to 450 qps (15m sustain at peak)
4) Cooldown: 15m back to baseline

Artifacts we expect:
- Aggregated latency CSV (p50/p95/p99) by 30s window
- Token-level tail latency logs (latency-run-20260910.log)
- Telemetry heatmap (telemetry-heatmap-20260910.png)
- Short incident notes if any 5xx or OOMs observed

Pre-run checklist (short):
- Provide test API keys + source IPs to allowlist (we can provide an ephemeral key if you prefer)
- Confirm dataset / prompt templates used (to match token distributions)
- If you plan to use multiple regions, call that out — cross-region latency is not part of this acceptance run

Can you confirm the two SRE contacts who will run the tests and a preferred start date/time? If Sep 13 works we'll schedule a kickoff and reserve telemetry review with Marissa.

Thanks — attaching the xlsx.

—Avery

Subject: Post-run artifacts: steady-state + peak run (Sep 10 internal test)

Hi team — we completed an internal smoke/pass of the run on Sep 10 (attached logs and heatmap). Highlights:
- Steady-state (60m at 150 qps): p50=32ms, p95=110ms, p99=280ms — acceptable
- Peak ramp (simulated to 420 qps): p50=58ms, p95=190ms, p99=520ms — note the P99 exceeds your 300ms target during sustained peak
- We saw increased token generation tail at the 28–30 minute mark of the ramp; attached latency-run-20260910.log includes per-request traces for samples that hit the P99 bucket

Questions:
1) Is the P99 > 300ms at peak a hard fail or a negotiated tolerance during initial go-live?
2) Any quick config knobs we can flip (batch window, kv cache policy) before Sep 13 to reduce tail?

We can push a second run on Sep 12 evening if that helps.

Thanks — attaching logs and heatmap.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole
SRE Lead, Triton Logistics
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@tritonlogistics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@tritonlogistics.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-run artifacts: steady-state + peak run (Sep 10 internal test)

Ethan — thanks for the artifacts and the clear notes. Quick readout and action grid: 

Assessment:
- Baseline run meets acceptance (good news).
- Peak run shows elevated tail at p99 (520ms) — most of the outliers are correlated with cache misses and a small number of OOM-retries recorded in the traces.

Immediate mitigations (before Sep 13 run):
1) Increase batch window from 8ms -> 12ms for the peak ramp only (expected ~8–12% improvement in p99 tail for our model family)
2) Enable aggressive KV warmup: preload top-10 prompt templates during warmup phase (Marissa will provide the script)
3) Add one temporary worker node (short-term burst) for the 15m peak sustain to reduce per-node queueing (Ben, please advise on provisioning)

Acceptance decision / tolerance: 
- For onboarding signoff we require: steady-state pass + peak p95 within 150% of target and p99 <= 600ms for an initial go-live.
- Final strict SLA (p99 <= 300ms) will be enforced post a 30-day stabilization window once production telemetry is observed.

Next steps:
- Marissa: schedule 09/13 09:00 PDT telemetry review and provide KV warmup script.
- Neha: confirm ephemeral key & allowlist updated (complete before 09/12 18:00 PDT).
- Ben: confirm short-term burst node provisioning and PO trigger if needed.
- Ethan/Priya: if you can re-run Sep 12 evening with the two config tweaks we recommended, we can give a green-light during the 09/13 review.

Thanks team — we'll use the Drive link for final artifacts and I'll draft the acceptance note once telemetry is validated.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
